Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

controversial adjective

also controversy, disputed, contested, debatable, in dispute, a controversial question, open to question

classical

Cic. Div. 2.104: quod dubium contrōversumque sit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Leg. 1.52: rēs contrōversa et plēna dissēnsiōnis inter doctissimōs (Lewis & Short)

contrōversus, contrōversa, contrōversum

adjective, declension

disputed, controversial

What is the subject of dispute: a question, a right, a piece of land. It does not mean “quarrelsome” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • in contrōversiā esse — be in dispute, be controversial

    phrase · also used · classical · Liv. 40.34.14: agrum, quī in contrōversiā erat (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Or. 2.291: rem in contrōversiam vocāre (Lewis & Short)

    contrōversia is the dispute itself, a controversy; in contrōversiam venīre is “to become controversial”, in contrōversiam vocāre “to call in question”.

  • contrōversiālis, contrōversiāle — controversial

    adjective, declension · avoid · late Latin · Sid. Ep. 7.9 (Lewis & Short)

    Late Latin; the classical word is contrōversus.

Examples

  • rēs contrōversa et plēna dissēnsiōnis inter doctissimōs

    a controversial matter, full of disagreement among the most learnedCic. Leg. 1.52 (Lewis & Short)

  • Rēs contrōversa est; nōn omnēs idem sentiunt.

    It’s a controversial question; not everyone thinks the same.composed

See also argument, doubt, opinion.

SourcesLewis & Short: controversus · Lewis & Short: controversia · Lewis & Short: controversialis
